prompt: During a heavy storm, rainwater runs down a bare hillside. The moving water carries loose soil down the slope and into a stream. What is the process that moved the soil?
explanation: Erosion is the moving of soil and rock pieces by water, wind or ice. Here running water carried loose soil away.

prompt: Large deposits of copper ore are found in only a few regions of the world. Most places have almost none. Which statement best explains this pattern?
choices: Copper ore forms in a few years wherever rain soaks into the soil.
Copper was once spread evenly, but people have mined it out of most places.
Ore forms only where past geologic processes concentrated the metal.
Living things make copper ore, so it builds up only under old forests.
correct_answer: Ore forms only where past geologic processes concentrated the metal.
explanation: Mineral deposits are uneven because they formed where processes such as cooling magma or moving hot water gathered metal in rock long ago.

distractor_rationales.choice: Copper ore forms in a few years wherever rain soaks into the soil.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: mineral resources form quickly and anywhere; ore takes very long and needs special conditions

distractor_rationales.choice: Copper was once spread evenly, but people have mined it out of most places.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: human use caused the uneven pattern; deposits were uneven before mining began

distractor_rationales.choice: Living things make copper ore, so it builds up only under old forests.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: all Earth resources come from living things; metal ore forms by geologic processes, not from life

real_world_check: Mineral resources are unevenly distributed because past geologic processes concentrated them in particular places.

prompt: A warm, humid air mass sits over a town. A cold, dry air mass moves in quickly and pushes in underneath it. Which prediction about the town's weather is best?
choices: The two air masses will blend at once, and the weather will not change.
The cold air will rise over the warm air and bring clear, warm skies.
The air may turn drier and clearer, because cold air holds more water vapor.
The warm air will be pushed upward, so clouds and rain are likely to form soon.
correct_answer: The warm air will be pushed upward, so clouds and rain are likely to form soon.
explanation: Dense cold air wedges under warm humid air and lifts it. As the warm air rises it cools, its water vapor condenses, and clouds and rain form along the front.

distractor_rationales.choice: The two air masses will blend at once, and the weather will not change.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: air masses mix evenly when they meet; they stay separate and form a front where weather changes

distractor_rationales.choice: The cold air will rise over the warm air and bring clear, warm skies.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: cold air rises; cold air is denser and sinks under warm air

distractor_rationales.choice: The air may turn drier and clearer, because cold air holds more water vapor.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: cold air holds more water vapor than warm air; warm air holds more

real_world_check: At a cold front, denser cold air lifts warm moist air, which cools and forms clouds and often rain.

prompt: Before many volcanic eruptions, instruments record the ground near the volcano bulging upward and many small earthquakes. Scientists use these signs to warn people. Which statement best explains why these signs often come before an eruption?
choices: Rising magma must push rock aside, so the ground bulges and cracks.
Eruptions follow a fixed schedule, and these signs always mark the date.
Sunlight heats the mountain, and it swells and shakes before erupting.
Heavy rain soaks into the volcano and makes it swell and shake.
correct_answer: Rising magma must push rock aside, so the ground bulges and cracks.
explanation: Magma moving up toward the surface takes up space, so it pushes the ground up and breaks rock, causing small earthquakes before it erupts.

distractor_rationales.choice: Eruptions follow a fixed schedule, and these signs always mark the date.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: volcanoes erupt on a regular schedule; eruptions are irregular, which is why monitoring is needed

distractor_rationales.choice: Sunlight heats the mountain, and it swells and shakes before erupting.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: heat from the Sun drives eruptions; the heat and pressure come from magma inside Earth

distractor_rationales.choice: Heavy rain soaks into the volcano and makes it swell and shake.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: weather causes the bulging and quakes; they come from magma moving underground

real_world_check: Ground swelling and swarms of small earthquakes at a volcano are caused by magma moving upward and are used to forecast eruptions.

prompt: Suppose Earth's axis were not tilted at all, but Earth still spun once a day and orbited the Sun once a year. Think about a town halfway between the equator and the North Pole. Which prediction is best?
choices: The town would always have its longest days in June, as it does now.
Summers would still be warm there, since distance to the Sun causes seasons.
The town would get about 12 hours of daylight on every single day of the year.
The town would have six months of daylight and then six months of night.
correct_answer: The town would get about 12 hours of daylight on every single day of the year.
explanation: Without tilt, the Sun would always be over the equator, so the line between day and night would pass through both poles and every town would get equal day and night all year.

distractor_rationales.choice: The town would always have its longest days in June, as it does now.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: day length changes for reasons other than tilt; without tilt day length would not change through the year

distractor_rationales.choice: Summers would still be warm there, since distance to the Sun causes seasons.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: seasons come from Earth's distance to the Sun; they come from the tilt of the axis

distractor_rationales.choice: The town would have six months of daylight and then six months of night.
distractor_rationales.fault: misconception: long polar days happen at every latitude; they happen only near the poles and only because of tilt

real_world_check: With no axial tilt the Sun stays over the equator, so away from the poles day and night would each last about 12 hours all year.
